actions.description: hamilton: cite Broadway Journal post(s) quoting AG-filed financials (BRO-6160)

actions.oldValue: Recouped its $12.5M Broadway capitalization ~8 months after first preview (Jul 2015 → Mar 2016; often misreported as 10 weeks). By mid-2016 grossing ~$600k/week in profit. Multiple productions worldwide; estimated total profit exceeds $1B.
actions.newValue: Recouped its $12.5M Broadway capitalization ~8 months after first preview (Jul 2015 → Mar 2016; often misreported as 10 weeks). By mid-2016 grossing ~$600k/week in profit. Multiple productions worldwide; estimated total profit exceeds $1B. AG-filed figures (Broadway Journal Apr 25 2018, Apr 26 2018, Jul 7 2020): distributed over $102M profit through Nov 2017; weekly operating profit averaged $1.15M in the year to July 2017 (48% of box office); $72M distributed in the year to July 2019 (producers take half of adjusted net profit); the Broadway producers also earned $10M of royalties, office charges and off-the-top profit in 2018-19. Per the Apr 2018 post the production recouped six months after opening night (recoupedDate left unchanged, within the ~8 months from first preview already recorded).
actions.description: hamilton: record AG-sourced figures (BRO-6160)

newValue.excerpt: The $9.4M production distributed $81M of profits from its first four years on Broadway, per financial statements filed with the state; weekly expenses excluding royalties averaged $760,000 in the 12 months to Feb 2015.

actions.description: book-of-mormon: cite Broadway Journal post(s) quoting AG-filed financials (BRO-6160)

actions.oldValue: Recouped in ~9 months. Multiple touring and international productions. Investors received multiple returns. Received $9.9M SVOG grant (per NY Business Journal Jul 2021).
actions.newValue: Recouped in ~9 months. Multiple touring and international productions. Investors received multiple returns. Received $9.9M SVOG grant (per NY Business Journal Jul 2021). AG-filed figures (Broadway Journal Feb 27 2021, Sep 22 2021, Apr 15 2016): paid out $81M of adjusted net profit over its first four years on Broadway; weekly expenses excluding royalties averaged $760,000 in the 12 months to Feb 2015 (the last year available); about $3M of royalties paid to workshop cast on the Broadway run (FOIL). Conflict noted, not resolved: those posts give production costs of $9.4M while the recorded capitalization is $11.4M (Hollywood Reporter); capitalization left unchanged.

actions.description: cabaret-2024: cite Broadway Journal post(s) quoting AG-filed financials (BRO-6160)

actions.oldValue: Closed Oct 2025 without recouping. Actual capitalization $24.25M (not $26M). $7.5M of investor money used to convert Kit Kat Club venue owned by ATG (the lead producer's parent company). Active investor lawsuit alleging producers used investor funds to improve their own real estate. Weekly nut $1.5M proved unsustainable. Investors received 0% recovery. Playbill (Sep 10, 2025): the producers said the production "has not been in a position fiscally to make any distribution to investors." https://playbill.com/article/facing-lawsuit-cabaret-producers-say-they-are-not-able-to-repay-investors

newValue.excerpt: MRB Musical LLC had returned 70 percent of its $28M capitalization to investors as of May 31, 2022, per papers filed with NY AG; $15M performance disruption insurance plus $10M SVOG exceeded the $18M spent shuttering and reopening.

actions.description: moulin-rouge: cite Broadway Journal post(s) quoting AG-filed financials (BRO-6160)

actions.oldValue: Recouped ~3 years after opening (Nov 2022, per SEC filing via Broadway News). Has grossed $194M+ on Broadway. Closing July 26, 2026 after 7 years (2,265 regular performances + 24 previews). Will be 36th longest-running show in Broadway history. Received $9.9M SVOG grant.
actions.newValue: Recouped ~3 years after opening (Nov 2022, per SEC filing via Broadway News). Has grossed $194M+ on Broadway. Closing July 26, 2026 after 7 years (2,265 regular performances + 24 previews). Will be 36th longest-running show in Broadway history. Received $9.9M SVOG grant. Per papers filed with NY AG (Broadway Journal Jun 11 2022): MRB Musical LLC had returned 70% of its $28M capitalization as of May 31 2022, helped by $15M of performance-disruption insurance proceeds and $10M of federal SVOG relief, which exceeded the $18M spent shuttering (Mar 2020) and reopening (Sep 2021). Consistent with the later Nov 2022 recoupment.

actions.description: harry-potter: cite Broadway Journal post(s) quoting AG-filed financials (BRO-6160)

actions.oldValue: Most expensive play ever to recoup, but investor returns are minimal. Per Broadway Journal (Boroff, Dec 2025), only $2.3M in profit distributions to investors (6% return over 7 years). High insider profit share (31% of net profits), $34M+ in theater rent to ATG, and $10M+ in producer royalties/fees absorbed most of the $456M gross. Posted $3.5M operating loss year ending Feb 2025. [Merged from duplicate harry-potter-2021 entry: Record-breaking $68 million investment for Broadway nonmusical play, primarily for theater renovations and production setup. Show opened in 2018 and remains open, but no recoupment information available.]

actions.description: king-kong-2018: cite Broadway Journal post(s) quoting AG-filed financials (BRO-6160)

actions.oldValue: Spectacle musical featuring a 20-foot, 2,000-pound animatronic puppet. Opened Nov 2018, closed Aug 2019 after 324 performances. Most expensive Broadway debut of its season at $35-36.5M (SEC filing). Weekly costs $1M+ due to massive puppet and crew. Only hit breakeven during holiday peaks. Grossed $36.71M total — barely equal to its budget. Near-total loss.

entry.notes: Per financial statements filed with NY State (Broadway Journal Apr 20 2021): weekly expenses exceeded $1.3M in some weeks of the 2017 Bette Midler revival. Per financial papers (Aug 23 2018): Jerry Herman and the Michael Stewart estate received a one-time $350,000 fee, 20% of weekly operating profit and 10% of net profit after recoupment. Investors reportedly earned a 5% profit by Aug 2018 (people familiar, not an AG figure). Outcome label left TBD pending a cited capitalization.

actions.description: in-transit-2016: add entry from AG-budget figures (BRO-6160)

entry.notes: Per a budget filed with the NY AG in summer 2016 (Broadway Journal Feb 2 2017): the production needed minimum weekly sales of $439,000 to pay expenses (includes credit card commissions and other extras that count toward League grosses); lead producer Janet Rosen said actual breakeven was below $400,000 because of conservative budgeting. Sales the week before were $338,000. Capitalized at just under $7M. Closed Feb 2017 without a reported recoupment.
